verdicts.reason: Quotes verified literally. meta/competitive-landscape.md:3 reads '> Status: `[DEEP]` — completed `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18.' and meta/constraints.md:3-4 reads '> Status: `[DEEP]` — all constraint categories resolved during `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18.' The pipeline key file contradicts both: ideation-index.md:94 '| Competitive Landscape | ... | `[PARTIAL]` |' and :95 '| Constraints | ... | `[PARTIAL]` |'. Checked for a reconciling convention and found none: grep over ideation-index.md returns PARTIAL only at :66, :94, :95, :154, :171, :210 — none of which defines a meta-document status legend, and the file carries no status legend section. The other four meta rows agree with their own headers (ideation-index.md:91, :92, :93, :96). Tested the obvious candidate discriminator — 'PARTIAL because open questions remain' — and it fails: competitive-landscape.md:98-105 has three open questions AND its header says [DEEP], while personas.md:165 also carries an Open Questions table and is [DEEP] in both places. So open questions cannot be what distinguishes the two [PARTIAL] rows. Neither statement carries a marker acknowledging the other, and status is what downstream reads to decide whether a meta document is consumable.

Quotes are accurate — constraints.md:199 does read 'hire → do the work → capture credit + split at source → on one identity' — but the correction is not absent, it is six lines below inside the same § v1 subsection and is explicitly dated and attributed: constraints.md:205 '| 02 | Credits & Attribution | the wedge — capture at the **first sharing moment** (D-70, 2026-07-22; capture-at-source is the *direction*, not the v1 claim — see § Project Surfaces, Desktop row) | 9 |'. The finding concedes this. The disambiguation is not silent, it is signed. It is reinforced three further times in the unit: problem-statement.md:47 marks rung 2 '**Not v1, and not authorised.** ... The **direction**, not the current claim.'; problem-statement.md:49-51 states the honest v1 claim; constraints.md:292 makes the Desktop row a prohibition. Line 199 is prose framing of the wedge; line 205 is the normative domain row. No implementer reading § v1 reaches 'build in-DAW capture' when the very next table row and the Project Surfaces section both forbid it. Two competent readers converge.

Quotes verified verbatim at personas.md:79, :81, :86, and grep confirms no D-70 marker anywhere in personas.md. But the divergence does not follow. personas.md declares its own consumption scope at :4 — 'Consumed by: every domain index Role Matrix (24), every feature file Role Lens' — it is a persona document (pain, workaround, success criteria, adoption constraint), not the capture-mechanism authority. The mechanism is stated normatively, twice, with dates: constraints.md:293 assigns the Tier 1 and Tier 2 cards to 'PWA web push plus the in-app surface' in v1, constraints.md:292 makes locally-installed client software 'NOT AUTHORISED', and constraints.md:319 pre-empts the exact reading the finding fears — 'DAW close is unavailable as a trigger.' personas.md:79 'split agreed before the session file closes' is a temporal success target, not a trigger specification, and :81 'Their work happens inside a DAW, not a browser' is a statement about user behaviour and adoption risk — the design pressure D-70's low-friction push card answers — not a claim about what v1 ships. A spec writer cannot build DAW-close capture from a persona row while constraints.md forbids the binary and names the trigger set.

Both quotes verified — competitive-landscape.md:82-85 and problem-statement.md:105, :112. But the deferral is well-formed on every axis the rule requires: problem-statement.md:112 is '| Q-02 | [OWNER] Is the lock-in **earned** or **hostile**? If a user leaves, what do they take? (Data portability is a cross-cut — and a values decision.) | User | `/create-prd` |' — marker, named owner (User), named target stage (/create-prd) — and problem-statement.md:105 cross-links it from DT-04 ('⏳ DEFERRED ... See Q-02'). Nothing is malformed. The two texts are also not the same statement: competitive-landscape.md § Moat is strategic positioning prose asserting an intent ('the moat is the accumulating, verified record'), while Q-02 asks the owner to ratify the values decision and settle *what a leaver takes* — the specific, unanswered half. The 'data they could export' clause sits inside a contrastive construction ('doesn't lose access to *data they could export*; they lose the *provenance*') whose point is what is NOT portable; reading it as a ratified portability commitment overstates it, and the portability cross-cut is exactly what Q-02 routes to /create-prd.

Verified: grep of headers in cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md returns no Open Questions section, and the two inline 'Open Q' strings sit at :123 and :124 as quoted. The claim that fails is 'nothing routes them to a stage or a decider.' Both rows are Section-1 rows, and Section 1 carries an explicit file-level route in two places: :7-9 '**Downstream contract**: `/create-prd` (architecture + shared-mechanism registry), `/decompose-architecture` (domain/shard boundaries), and `/audit-ambiguity` inherit this file' and :268 '**Bottom line for D-17:** ... Commission the Section-1 mechanism extractions in `/create-prd`'. The stage that resolves 'shared cross-cut vs education-owned instances' and 'push-at-purchase vs pull-as-of-at-release' is therefore named. The file demonstrably does per-item routing where it differs from the default (:265 'decide at `/decompose-architecture`', :259 'escalate to `/create-prd` for an explicit keep-or-fold decision'), so the default route is a convention, not an omission. :85's 'Owner ambiguous by design' is a deliberate declaration, not untracked drift. Both questions are visibly flagged open, so no implementer silently invents a data model — they escalate to the commissioned stage.

The arithmetic is quoted correctly — :5 '101 boundary problems (`bp`)', :226 'The 101 boundary problems were classified into', :239-240 'The fix for ~85 of the 101 is mechanism extraction per Section 1', and the table at :250-253 summing ~10 + 2 + ~65 + ~8 = ~85 against a class of ~65. It is a real slip in a descriptive statistic. It is not an ambiguity that forces invention, because nothing normative in the section is sized by that number. The section's operative outputs are enumerated by name, not by count: :268-272 '**Bottom line for D-17:** keep 24 domains. Commission the Section-1 mechanism extractions in `/create-prd` (especially the Money & Exploitation schema layer, the Split-Capture/session-close moment, the Entitled-Party Delivery Layer, the Graded-Attestation primitive, and the Outbound Deliverability Commons). Carry **one** genuine domain-merge decision forward — **07/08 (Overdub)** — and four shared-owner/relocation decisions'. The extraction scope is the Section-1 mechanism tables (:30-125); the merge scope is the eight named rows at :259-266. Every count in the table is hedged with '~'. Both the 65 and the 85 reading yield the identical verdict, the identical extraction list and the identical five carried decisions, so no two implementers scope different work.

Quotes verified at constraints.md:160-161, :165-167, :168. But 'no value' here is a ratified owner decision, not a gap: :158 '> Confirmed 2026-07-18, `/ideate-validate`' and :168 '- **Not a hard ceiling number** — "keep it cheap" is the rule, no fixed $/month cap set.' A deliberately capless posture is decided, so the absence of a `[PENDING — <stage>]` marker is correct — the comparison with the Performance axis (:273 'Hard budget set at `/create-prd-compile`') is a comparison with a genuinely deferred axis, not a missing marker. The hard case is also routed, not left to the implementer: :162 '- **Implication for `/create-prd-stack`**' makes spend-shape an explicit input to the stack stage, and 'must be justified against a cheaper edge/managed alternative' is a comparison obligation discharged at that stage against the already-locked Cloudflare Pages + Workers + Supabase stack (:162-164) — a named baseline to justify against, which the finding treats as absent. No implementer invents a hosting bill here; adding a fixed monthly floor is an architecture decision the tree sends to /create-prd-stack.

All six 'Measurable:' quotes verified at personas.md:52, :79, :104, :132 and counterparties.md:50, :78, and they are indeed directional. The load-bearing claim — 'Every success metric in the unit is directional ... there is no counter-example' — fails because the project's success metrics are not in meta/. ideation-index.md:156 routes rubric dimension 5 explicitly: '| 5 | Success Measurability | ✅ | Each metric has a method + target; wedge metrics numeric (split-capture ≥60% @ 6mo, capture <7d); baseline-set + hard SLOs deferred to `/create-prd-compile`. [vision.md](../vision.md) |'. Checked the target: vision.md:153 'Each metric below has a **measurement method** and a **target**', vision.md:161 '**Target: ≥ 60% within 6 months of v1 launch**', :164 '**Target: < 7 days median**', :171 '**Target: ≥ 50% verified**', with the remainder marked *(baseline-set)* (:169, :177, :182) and latency/availability deferred to the performance budget (:186). The persona 'Measurable:' clauses are per-persona qualitative indicators sitting beside qualitative Success Criteria prose; the falsifiable metric set with methods, numeric targets and a named deferral stage exists and is cross-referenced from the pipeline key file.
